cards.text: This psalm doesn't ease in, friend. First word out of the gate: Hallelujah! The writer isn't named, but he's calling out to the servants of the LORD, and he is NOT using his indoor voice.

cards.question: The psalm writer calls out to the servants of the LORD. What does he tell them to do?

answers.text: Praise the name of the LORD
Go up to the house of God

cards.question: True or false: the psalm writer says the name of the LORD should be blessed only on feast days.

cards.text: Then he zooms out. WAY out. He pictures the sun coming up on one edge of the world and going down on the other.

cards.question: From where the sun rises to where it sets, the name of the LORD is ___.

cards.text: Sunrise to sunset, friend. Back in the junk drawer, I threw a PARTY over five seconds of kitchen light when somebody opened it looking for tape.

cards.question: The LORD is exalted over all the nations. True or false: the psalm writer says His glory reaches the heavens and goes no higher.

cards.text: Then comes the question this whole psalm hangs on: "Who is like the LORD our God, the One enthroned on high?"

cards.question: The psalm writer asks, "Who is like the LORD our God, the One enthroned on high?" What answer is he expecting?

cards.text: Nobody's raising a hand on that one. Now listen to what the One enthroned on high does next.

cards.question: The One enthroned on high ___ Himself to behold the heavens and the earth.

cards.text: He's so high, He humbles Himself just to look at the heavens and the earth, and meanwhile I have to hop up on my gold base to see over a MIXING BOWL. And He doesn't just look.

cards.question: The LORD raises the ___ from the dust.

cards.text: He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the dump. The DUMP, friend, and I thought the back of a junk drawer was rock bottom.

cards.question: The LORD lifts the needy from the dump. Where does He seat them?

answers.text: With the princes of His people
At the gate of the city
Among the servants of the king

cards.text: From the dump to a seat with nobles is like going from the mailroom to the corner office in one afternoon. Then the psalm closes with one more picture, inside a home.

cards.question: Who does the LORD settle in her home as a joyful mother to her children?
True or false: the psalm writer closes Psalm 113 with Hallelujah.

findings.problem: Card 6 tells nothing new from the passage. It repeats 'Sunrise to sunset' from card 4 and then adds a joke. It's a joke-only recap card, and its citation of Psalm 113:3 covers no new content.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new drawer moment: throwing a PARTY over five seconds of kitchen light. The backstory says the light was bittersweet and that everyone held their breath, unsure whether they'd be used or thrown out. It also says he didn't joke at all during his low period in the drawer. Jokes may invent small moments only around his bakery.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The core action of Psalm 113:3 is the LORD's name being praised everywhere the sun goes. The joke's action is celebrating a few seconds of light. The comparison picks up the sunlight image, not the praising action, so the link doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Card 10 adds no passage content. 'Nobody's raising a hand on that one' recaps the answer to card 9, and 'Now listen to what the One enthroned on high does next' is filler. It cites Psalm 113:5 without telling any of it.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the exact verb of Psalm 113:6 ('humbles'). Card 10 gives no context to reason from. Coming right after verses about the LORD being exalted, 'exalts' is just as likely a pick. This tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'exalts' is arguable. Psalm 113:4 says 'The LORD is exalted over all the nations,' so a baker could argue the One enthroned on high exalting Himself fits the passage.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: 'Hallelujah' first appears in Psalm 113:1, where card 1 told it. Card 18 asks about its second appearance in Psalm 113:9.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.
